hotspots.title: The transmitter
hotspots.text: Figure 1 is the sending side. A variable frequency carrier oscillator lets the transmitter change from one radio frequency to another at intervals.

VARIABLE FREQUENCY CARRIER OSCILLATOR
secret communication systems involving the use of carrier waves of different frequencies

hotspots.region_note: Fig. 1 paper roll running between two spools and a motor
hotspots.title: A player-piano roll
hotspots.text: This paper roll is the secret key. The inventors borrowed the idea from player pianos: a piano roll may have 88 rows of holes, so their system could use 88 different frequencies.

evidence.exact_span: we contemplate employing records of the type used for many years in player pianos
In a conventional player piano record there may be 88 rows of perforations, and in our system such a record would permit the use of 88 different carrier frequencies

hotspots.region_note: Fig. 2 boxes: selector, amplifier, detector
hotspots.title: The receiver
hotspots.text: Figure 2 is the receiving side. A matching roll changes its tuning at the same moments, so only a receiver with the same record can follow the signal.

evidence.exact_span: Fig. 2 is a schematic diagram of the apparatus at a receiving station;
employs a pair of synchronous records, one at the transmitting station and one at the receiving station, which change the tuning of the transmitting and receiving apparatus from time to time
without knowledge of the records an enemy would be unable to determine at what frequency a controlling impulse would be sent

hotspots.region_note: Fig. 3: dashed boxes labelled transmitting station and torpedo

hotspots.text: Figure 3 starts the motors at both ends at the same moment: the transmitting station and the torpedo. Without the records, an enemy could not tell which frequency the next command would use.

artifacts.transcription:
J. W. DAVIS. Fastening Pocket-Openings. No. 139,121. Patented May 20, 1873.
Fig. 1. [Letters on the drawing: A once, and b five times.]
Witnesses [two signatures; the first is illegible] C. M. Richardson
Inventor Jacob W. Davis per Dewey & Co. Attys
AM. PHOTO-LITHOGRAPHIC CO. N.Y. (OSBORNE'S PROCESS)
artifacts.related_text:
UNITED STATES PATENT OFFICE. JACOB W. DAVIS, OF RENO, NEVADA, ASSIGNOR TO HIMSELF AND LEVI STRAUSS & COMPANY, OF SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA. IMPROVEMENT IN FASTENING POCKET-OPENINGS. Specification forming part of Letters Patent No. 139,121, dated May 20, 1873; application filed August 9, 1872.
My invention relates to a fastening for pocket-openings, whereby the sewed seams are prevented from ripping or starting from frequent pressure or strain thereon; and it consists in the employment of a metal rivet or eyelet at each edge of the pocket-opening, to prevent the ripping of the seam at those points.
A is the side seam in a pair of pants, drawers, or other article of wearing apparel, which terminates at the pockets; and b b represent the rivets at each edge of the pocket opening.
The seams are usually ripped or started by the placing of the hands in the pockets and the consequent pressure or strain upon them.
To strengthen this part I employ a rivet, eyelet, or other equivalent metal stud, b, which I pass through a hole at the end of the seam, so as to bind the two parts of cloth together, and then head it down upon both sides so as to firmly unite the two parts.
I am aware that rivets have been used for securing seams in shoes
As a new article of manufacture, a pair of pantaloons having the pocket-openings secured at each edge by means of rivets, substantially in the manner described and shown, whereby the seams at the points named are prevented from ripping, as set forth.

artifacts.alt: Einstein's 1936 Declaration of Intention form, with his photograph and his signature.
artifacts.transcription:
TRIPLICATE (To be given to declarant) No. 1442 UNITED STATES OF AMERICA DECLARATION OF INTENTION (Invalid for all purposes seven years after the date hereof)
United States of America District of New Jersey ss: In the District Court of The United States at Trenton, N. J.
I, Dr. Albert Einstein now residing at 112 Mercer St., Princeton Mercer N.J. occupation Professor, aged 56 years, do declare on oath that my personal description is: Sex Male, color White, complexion Fair, color of eyes Brown color of hair Grey, height 5 feet 7 inches; weight 175 pounds; visible distinctive marks none race Hebrew; nationality German
I was born in Ulm Germany on March 14 1879 I am married. The name of my wife [a typed word struck out] is Elsa we were married on April 6th 1917, at Berlin Germany; she or he was born at Hechinge[n] Germany, on January 18, 1877, entered the United States at New York N.Y., on June 3, 1935, for permanent residence therein, and now resides at With me I have 2 children, and the name, date and place of birth, and place of residence of each of said children are as follows: Albert born 5-14-1905 and Eduard born 6-28-1910 both born and reside in Switzerland
I have not heretofore made a declaration of intention: my last foreign residence was Bermuda Great Britain I emigrated to the United States of America from Bermuda Great Britain my lawful entry for permanent residence in the United States was at New York N.Y. under the name of Albert Einstein, on June 3, 1935 on the vessel SS Queen of Bermuda
I will, before being admitted to citizenship, renounce forever all allegiance and fidelity to any foreign prince, potentate, state, or sovereignty, and particularly, by name, to the prince, potentate, state, or sovereignty of which I may be at the time of admission a citizen or subject; I am not an anarchist; I am not a polygamist nor a believer in the practice of polygamy; and it is my intention in good faith to become a citizen of the United States of America and to reside permanently therein; and I certify that the photograph affixed to the duplicate and triplicate hereof is a likeness of me: So help me God.
[signature] Albert Einstein
Subscribed and sworn to before me in the office of the Clerk of said Court, at Trenton, N. J. this 15th day of January anno Domini 1936. Certification No. 3-120742 from the Commissioner of Immigration and Naturalization showing the lawful entry of the declarant for permanent residence on the date stated above, has been received by me.
George T. Cranmer Clerk of the U. S. District Court. By [signature] Deputy Clerk.
[photograph, signed] Albert Einstein (The seal of the court will be impressed so as to cover a portion of the photograph)
Form 2202-L-A U. S. DEPARTMENT OF LABOR IMMIGRATION AND NATURALIZATION SERVICE No. 5773
artifacts.transcription_note: Typed entries as they appear on the form, including the categories the 1930s form required. [n] marks a letter partly hidden by an overprinted label. Handwritten signatures are marked [signature].

artifacts.transcription:
(Shanghai C-39) (Approved by Department January 10, 1924) AMERICAN CONSULATE-GENERAL SHANGHAI, CHINA. July 20, 1935. 15-16 PRECIS OF INVESTIGATION.
Name: Pe, Ieoh-ming ([name in Chinese characters]) Nationality: Chinese. Class: Student. Passport Visa No. 13/1935-36. Section 6 Certificate issued by the Commissioner of Public Safety at Shanghai, China, on July 12, 1935. Visa granted by this Consulate-General on: July 13, 1935. Bearer's birthplace: Canton, China. Family (ages by ---- reckoning): Not married.
Review of bearer's education: Graduated from St. John's Middle School in 1934. For the past year has attended St. John's University.
Plans for education in the United States: Will attend the University of Pennsylvania for six years studying for A.M. degree.
Provision for financial support: Full support is to be provided by applicant's father, Tsuyee Pei, manager of the Bank of China, who is very well fixed finanacially.
Reference in the United States: Not acquainted.
Consular investigation and remarks: Examination has been made of the applicant who has presented a telegram accepting him as a student from the University of Pennsylvania; a letter from St. John's University stating that he is a student there and recommending him; a letter from his father guaranteeing full support.
[photograph, signed] Ieoh-ming Pe
Intended departure: Steamship: PRESIDENT COOLIDGE Sailing date: August 13, 1935 Port of entry: San Francisco.
[signature] James B. Pilcher American Vice Consul. 811.11 JBP/Jts
